| | Phone screenshot | Full-height review |

| Bounded by | Device viewport | Component's full content height |

2. **Parse from a file, not from an echoed string.** Write the response body to a file (e.g. `curl -o run.json`) and read the fields from it. This keeps the JSON valid, and it leaves you a record you can re-check if you lose track of which id is which.

3. **Carry the labels through your plan.** Write the update plan in terms of the labelled values, for example "send a chat message to project `<projectId>` targeting screen `<screenId>`", so each id's role is explicit at every step.

4. **Place each id by its type.** The project id goes in the URL path, as in `/api/v1/projects/:id/chat/messages`. The screen id goes wherever the endpoint contract asks for a screen reference. The supplied facts don't spell out that field, so confirm it in `endpoints.md` or the OpenAPI spec at `https://sleek.design/api/v1/spec.json` before building the call.

5. **Never infer type from the value.** If provenance is ever lost, don't guess from the string's shape or position. Go back to the saved response and re-read which field held it.
